allegations.text: Defendant University of Washington ("Defendant UW") is a public university, including a medical school and medical clinics, owned and operated by Defendant State of Washington. At all times material hereto, Defendant UW employed the individual healthcare providers identified in plaintiff's medical records, and is a health care provider within the meaning of RCW 7.70.020.
Defendants John Does 1-10 are individuals who provided care and treatment to plaintiff and whose identities will be learned during discovery.
Defendants Jane Does 1-10 are individuals who provided care and treatment to plaintiff and whose identities will be learned during discovery.
Plaintiff Jeremy Morton-Maxson is a natural person who was, at all times material hereto, a resident of King County, Washington.

Pursuant to RCW 4.92.100, plaintiff delivered a tort claim notice to Defendant UW on March 14, 2023, and 60 days have elapsed. Defendant UW acknowledged receipt of plaintiff's tort claim notice on March 20, 2023. Plaintiff has also filed a declaration regarding voluntary arbitration pursuant to RCW 7.70A.020. Any statutory prerequisites to the maintenance of this action have therefore been satisfied.
Jurisdiction and venue are proper in King County because the acts and omissions giving rise to the cause of action occurred in King County, Washington.

On or about August 17, 2022, plaintiff Jeremy Morton-Maxson had a tumor surgically removed from his bladder at Defendant UW's Northwest Main Operating Room after presenting with blood in his urine and a family history of bladder cancer.
Plaintiff's treating doctors noted that the tumor was "likely cancer" and that a pathologic review was necessary to determine the nature of the tumor.
Defendant UW lost the surgically removed tumor prior to conducting the requisite pathologic review, and left plaintiff without a clear diagnosis or care plan.

Defendant UW failed to have and follow proper policies, procedures, and training regarding safeguarding, maintenance, custody, and transportation of plaintiff's surgically removed tumor, and failed to properly train and supervise the providers and staff involved in plaintiff's care and treatment.
As a result of the negligence of defendants, plaintiff Jeremy Morton-Maxson has suffered and continues to suffer injuries and damages that are painful, progressive, and permanent.
Defendant UW and their employees are healthcare providers as defined by Chapter 7.70 RCW.
Defendant UW is liable for the negligent acts and omissions of their employees, agents, and staff under the doctrine of respondeat superior.

Defendant UW, individually and through its employees, agents, and staff, negligently failed to exercise the degree of care, skill, and learning of a reasonably prudent healthcare provider in the State of Washington, and this negligence was a proximate cause of the injuries and damages to the plaintiff.

In the alternative, healthcare providers John Does 1-10 and Jane Does 1-10 who provided care and treatment to plaintiff were apparent or ostensible agents of Defendant UW, and Defendant UW is liable for their acts under general rules of agency.

As a direct and proximate result of the conduct of the above-named defendants, Jeremy Morton-Maxson incurred general and special damages in an amount to be proven at trial, including but not limited to pain, suffering, mental anguish, emotional distress, inconvenience, disability, and loss of society and companionship.
